stem: Seven delegates are to be seated around a circular conference table. Two particular delegates, Arjun and Bhavna, insist on sitting next to each other. In how many ways can the seating be arranged?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Treat Arjun and Bhavna as one unit: 6 units around a circle = (6-1)! = 120. Arjun and Bhavna can swap within the unit: 2! = 2. Total = 120 x 2 = 1440.
Computed (6-1)! = 120 and multiplied by 6 instead of 2, or directly wrote 720, forgetting the internal swap of the pair.
Computed (6-1)! / 2 = 60 x ... or 5! = 120 then divided by a factor, confusing necklace formula with the constraint.
Computed (5-1)! x 2! x 2 = 48 x ... or another mis-grouping yielding 480.

explanation: Glue the constrained pair into a single block. This gives 6 objects to arrange around a circle: (6-1)! = 5! = 120 ways. The two people inside the block can switch places in 2! = 2 ways. Multiply: 120 x 2 = 1440.

explanation_sections.punchline: Bundle the inseparable pair into one block, count the circular arrangements of the resulting 6 objects, then restore internal order.
explanation_sections.approach: Classify: circular arrangement, together constraint. Step 1 - merge pair into 1 block: n reduces from 7 to 6. Step 2 - circular arrangements of 6 blocks: (6-1)! = 120. Step 3 - internal permutations of the 2-person block: 2! = 2. Multiply: 120 x 2 = 1440.
explanation_sections.lesson: Together constraint: merge into one block, reduce n by (block size - 1), then multiply by internal factorial.
explanation_sections.timing: 30 seconds: 5! x 2 = 120 x 2 = 1440. Trap: forgetting the internal swap gives only 120.
